# NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity — facts

> Source-anchored units about NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity: 11 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] MongoDB documents NoWritesPerformed starting in version 6.1: when both attempts fail without any write, the label distinguishes zero work from partial insertMany execution; earlier versions lacked this distinction. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/retryable-writes.md · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/7.0.md
- [statement] The retryable-writes specification selects the latest error indicating a write attempt when any such error exists, but the first error when all attempts are known no-ops. Thus a later NoWritesPerformed error must not replace an earlier ambiguous write error. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-14) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69295, https://github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/pull/3441
- [statement] Retryable execution is command-scoped: drivers assign separate transaction numbers to split write commands and reuse each command's transaction ID on retry. A zero-write failure for a later command therefore does not establish zero writes across the whole application bulk. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/crud/bulk-write.md
- [statement] A failed retry stops remaining split-batch execution even when ordered is false. Drivers are encouraged to expose intermediary results; client-level BulkWriteException defines optional partialResult for confirmed successes before the error. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/crud/bulk-write.md
- [statement] DRIVERS-2501 records an earlier all-NoWritesPerformed error sequence that could propagate null; the documented correction retains the first labeled error. The specification likewise initializes its saved error on the first failure. (high confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-2501 · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md
- [statement] Retryability is evaluated per command after batch splitting. If a retry fails, remaining operations stop even for unordered batches. Therefore a no-write result for the failed command cannot by itself establish zero effects across earlier commands in the logical batch. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/crud/bulk-write.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The Node.js driver's October 2022 NODE-4503 change explicitly throws the original error when a retry error carries NoWritesPerformed, providing an implementation example of preserving the earlier failure rather than reporting only the later no-op. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/pull/3441 · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69295

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A missing acknowledgment can leave a write's outcome unknown. Application-level replay of non-idempotent work can duplicate effects; a failed response alone is not proof of non-execution. (high confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-3-6-retryable-writes-retryable-writes/ · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://jepsen.io/analyses/jetcd-0.8.2
- [statement] A missing acknowledgement can leave a write successful but unknown to the client. Consequently, absence of NoWritesPerformed is not proof that a particular number of documents was inserted; the manual’s partial-work example must not be read as a universal converse. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/retryable-writes.md · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-3-6-retryable-writes-retryable-writes/, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md
- [statement] MongoClient.bulkWrite exceptions distinguish top-level errors, write-concern errors, individual write errors, and optional partialResult. Drivers must omit partialResult unless at least one successful write can be established; omission therefore does not prove that no write occurred. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/crud/bulk-write.md · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity
- [statement] Definite non-execution and unknown execution require different recovery decisions. Repeating a non-idempotent operation after an unknown outcome can duplicate effects; MongoDB retryable writes address this with shared operation identity between driver and server. (high confidence) — https://jepsen.io/analyses/jetcd-0.8.2 · keywords: NoWritesPerformed and retryable batch outcome ambiguity · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-3-6-retryable-writes-retryable-writes/, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/retryable-writes/retryable-writes.md
